title: Early Blight in Tomatoes
content: Dark spots with concentric rings on lower leaves signal early blight. Remove affected foliage immediately and apply copper-based fungicide. Water at the base to keep leaves dry and reduce spread.

title: Prevent Rice Blast
content: Rice blast causes diamond-shaped lesions on leaves and neck rot on panicles. Use resistant varieties, avoid excessive nitrogen, and apply tricyclazole or isoprothiolane at first sign of infection.

title: Manage Powdery Mildew
content: White powdery growth on leaves reduces photosynthesis. Improve air circulation through proper spacing, apply sulfur or neem oil weekly, and remove heavily infected plant parts.

title: Scout Fields Regularly
content: Walk your fields at least once a week during the growing season. Check the underside of leaves for eggs and early-stage pests. Early detection can reduce pesticide use by up to 40%.

title: Corn Leaf Blight Warning
content: Northern Corn Leaf Blight shows as long, cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on lower leaves. Rotate crops, use resistant hybrids, and apply fungicide at tasseling if humidity is high.

title: Potato Late Blight Action
content: Late blight thrives in cool, wet weather. Water-soaked lesions on leaves with white fungal growth at the margins. Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb preventatively. Destroy infected plants immediately.

title: Downy Mildew on Grapes
content: Yellow oil spots on upper leaf surface with white downy growth underneath. Prune for better airflow, apply copper-based sprays before rain events, and remove mummified berries after harvest.

title: Clean Equipment Between Fields
content: Plant pathogens spread easily through contaminated tools and machinery. Disinfect pruning shears, tillers, and sprayers between fields with a 10% bleach solution to prevent cross-contamination.
